darkScheme.note: Light is the designed default. Unlisted tokens keep their light value; the approve button text turns #08180f in dark. Board-lit literals (board-lamp-*, board-red-face, lit-green, focus-on-dark, on-yellow) are scheme-independent.

wordmark.purpose: "Orchestrator" beside the andon-tower mark in the rail.

title-sm.purpose: Headings inside a panel (diagnosis, inspector sub-blocks).

body.purpose: All running text; root size 15px; tabular figures throughout.

button.purpose: Buttons and tabs; 0.87rem on small buttons.

label-board.purpose: Andon board cell names, two-line clamp.

label-head.purpose: Uppercase table column heads; DAG stage labels at 0.76rem.

figure.purpose: Stat figures on the Workers page.

mono.purpose: IDs, worker names, feed timestamps, logs, JSON, definitions.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Settings dialog and toasts only; panels and the board stay flat.

shadows.name: lamp-edge
shadows.purpose: Outline of an unlit, paused or skipped lamp; an outline, not elevation.

shadows.name: stopped-rule
shadows.purpose: Red rule across the board foot when the line is stopped.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on buttons, chips, nav items.

motion.name: lamp-change
motion.purpose: Lamp fill and DAG plate colour changes; progress bar width.

motion.name: face-sweep
motion.purpose: A board cell face filling yellow or red as its lamp comes on.

motion.name: lamp-pulse
motion.purpose: Running lamps on the line, the board and DAG nodes breathe.

motion.name: lamp-call
motion.purpose: A gate awaiting a person calls faster.

motion.name: edge-flow
motion.purpose: DAG edge into a running step.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all animations and transitions collapse to 0.001ms

breakpoints.name: wide

breakpoints.name: detail
breakpoints.purpose: Run detail, I/O and editor go single column.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Overview top row and workflow rows stack.

breakpoints.name: rail-collapse

breakpoints.name: phone

narrative.overview:
Orchestrator is a production line. Workers pull work, a stuck station calls for help, and anyone can stop the line. The dashboard is the andon board hung over that line: a deep machine-green rail down the left, a near-black board band across the top, and below them a light shop-floor grey ground carrying paper-white work panels. Everything at rest is quiet. Colour comes on only where a station is running, waiting for a person, or broken, so the eye finds the problem before it reads a word.

The density is an operator's, not a brochure's: hairline-ruled tables, condensed board labels, tabular figures, step lamps in a row. Corners are nearly square, surfaces are flat, and depth comes from tone (ground, panel, sunk) instead of shadow. Motion is a lamp's: running lamps breathe, a gate waiting for a person blinks faster, and a board cell that needs you sweeps its whole face to yellow or red. Light is the designed default (a viewer on a laptop in daylight); a dark scheme follows the operating system and keeps every role.

The world was built to refuse the category default for AI dashboards: a navy ground with a purple accent and a grid of KPI cards.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed frame on every screen: machine-green rail (228px) and the andon board band.
Lamp colours are reserved for state; finished work goes quiet graphite.
Square lamps (2px corners) are the system's atom: badges, station rows, board cells, DAG nodes, chart keys and toasts all use them.
Barlow for UI, Barlow Semi Condensed for board labels, table heads and figures, JetBrains Mono only for machine text.
Flat, hairline-ruled panels at 3px corners; shadows only on what floats over the floor.

rules.name: The Lamp Reservation Rule
rules.body: Green, yellow, red and blue mean state and nothing else. They never decorate and never fill a primary action. Two exceptions are part of the world: the wordmark's andon tower, the one place red, yellow and green stand together at rest, and the verdict actions (Approve fills with green ink; Reject, Cancel run, Delete and Pause all execution take a red-ink outline).

rules.name: The Quiet Finish Rule
rules.body: Green means moving now. Work that has finished goes graphite, never green, so a screen of completed runs reads calm and the one running station stands out.

rules.name: The Whole Face Rule
rules.body: A board cell that needs a person lights its entire face (Signal Yellow for a gate, Line-Stop Red for a failure); every other cell carries only a small lamp. Stopping the line is the loudest state on the board: a 3px red rule across the board's foot.

rules.name: The Condensed Voice Rule
rules.body: Barlow Semi Condensed speaks only for the board, table heads, figures, counts, tags and DAG sublabels. It never sets running text or a page title, and its uppercase form stays on column heads and DAG labels.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what the machine wrote: IDs, timestamps, logs, JSON, definitions. A human-facing label never goes mono.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Rail and board are on every screen, and the board always shows every workflow plus the line cell. Pages add panels on the floor; they never replace the frame.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Panels, tables, cards and the board never cast shadows. If something needs separation, give it a rule or a tone step; only a dialog or toast lifts.

rules.name: The Square Lamp Rule
rules.body: A lamp is a square with 2px corners: filled when lit, an inset 1.5px outline when unlit, hatched when skipped, a hollow ink outline when paused. Never a circle, never a dot, never a pill.

dos: **Do** keep the rail and andon board on every screen, with every workflow represented as a board cell.
**Do** reserve green, yellow, red and blue for state (The Lamp Reservation Rule) and turn finished work graphite.
**Do** draw every status as a square lamp with 2px corners plus a label in the state's ink tone; never rely on colour alone.
**Do** use Machine Green (#1d3a32) for the primary action, and green-ink fill or red-ink outline only for verdicts and destructive actions.
**Do** keep panels flat, hairline-ruled and 3px-cornered on the Shop Floor ground; separate by tone and rules.
**Do** set figures, counts and table heads in Barlow Semi Condensed with tabular numerals, and put IDs, timestamps, logs and JSON in JetBrains Mono.
**Do** draw a state that spans a panel (approval gate, open run form) as a full-width band to the panel edges.
**Do** honour reduced motion: lamp breathing, face sweeps and edge flow all collapse to static.
donts: **Don't** build the category default: a navy dashboard with a purple accent and a grid of KPI cards. Figures live inside the panel that owns them, next to the chart or control they explain.
**Don't** use a lamp colour as decoration or a primary-button fill; outside the wordmark's tower, a lamp hue always names a state.
**Don't** use circles, dots or pills for lamps, counts or tags, or round anything past the dialog's 4px.
**Don't** add shadows to panels, tables or the board.
**Don't** lift the uppercase table-head style above page or panel titles as a kicker or eyebrow.
**Don't** set running text or page titles in the condensed face, or human labels in mono.
**Don't** mix icon families or use filled or glyph icons; Lucide line icons at 1.85 stroke only.
